chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about oil and butter, two units for one unit. He said, 'Hand to hand, there is no objection to it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no objection to it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for exchanging unequal amounts of the same commodity in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that exchanging two units of oil for one unit of butter is permissible provided the transaction is 'hand to hand' (yadan bi-yad). This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction where unequal quantities of the same commodity type are allowed if the condition of immediate exchange is met, thereby avoiding the prohibition of riba al-fadl. The emphasis on physical possession or immediate delivery underscores the practical application of trade laws in early Islamic markets.
